level1.text: An example household uses $3000\,\text{kWh}$ of electricity a year. The electricity is produced with hydropower, whose life-cycle emission factor is $24\,\text{g/kWh}$. How much carbon dioxide equivalent is produced per year by the household's electricity use? Give the answer in kilograms.

An electric sauna heater uses $3.0\,\text{kWh}$ of electricity in one sauna session. The electricity is produced with coal, whose life-cycle emission factor is $820\,\text{g/kWh}$. How much carbon dioxide equivalent is produced by one sauna session? Give the answer in kilograms.

An electric car uses $18\,\text{kWh}$ of electricity over a distance of $100\,\text{km}$. The electricity used to charge the car has been produced with wind power, whose life-cycle emission factor is $12\,\text{g/kWh}$. How much carbon dioxide equivalent is produced per $100\,\text{km}$? Give the answer in grams.

The life-cycle emission factor of rooftop panels is $41\,\text{g/kWh}$ and that of natural gas electricity is $490\,\text{g/kWh}$. Both produce the same amount of electricity. How many times as large is the emission of natural gas electricity compared with that of rooftop panels?

A washing machine and a tumble dryer together use $2.4\,\text{kWh}$ of electricity for one load of laundry. The electricity is produced with natural gas, whose life-cycle emission factor is $490\,\text{g/kWh}$. How much carbon dioxide equivalent is produced by one load of laundry? Give the answer in kilograms.

level2.text: A power plant that uses biomass produces $2.0\,\text{GWh}$ of electricity in a month. The life-cycle emission factor of biomass electricity is $230\,\text{g/kWh}$. How many tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent are produced by a month of electricity production? Give the answer in tonnes.

An example household uses $3600\,\text{kWh}$ of electricity a year. The electricity was first produced with coal ($820\,\text{g/kWh}$), but the household switches to buying wind electricity ($12\,\text{g/kWh}$). By how many tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent do the yearly emissions decrease? Give the answer in tonnes.

The electricity production of a small factory produced $12\,\text{t}$ of carbon dioxide equivalent during a year. The electricity was produced with natural gas, whose emission factor is $490\,\text{g/kWh}$. How much electricity did the factory produce? Give the answer in kilowatt-hours.

The emission factor for the burning of petrol is $69\,\text{g/MJ}$. Give the emission factor in the unit $\text{g/kWh}$, when $1\,\text{kWh} = 3.6\,\text{MJ}$. Only burning is counted, not the whole life cycle.

level3.text: A petrol car uses $6.0$ litres per $100\,\text{km}$. The energy content of petrol is $32\,\text{MJ/}\textsf{l}$ and the emission factor of burning is $69\,\text{g/MJ}$. An electric car uses $18\,\text{kWh}$ of electricity per $100\,\text{km}$. (The comparison is rough: for the petrol car only burning is counted, for the electric car the life-cycle emissions of the electricity.) At what emission factor of electricity would the emission of the electric car over $100\,\text{km}$ be equal to that of the petrol car? Give the answer in the unit $\text{g/kWh}$. What does the result tell about the benefit of the electric car if the electricity is produced with coal?

An example city needs $100\,\text{GWh}$ of electricity a year and compares two ways. A solar park produces about $0.50\,\text{GWh}$ of electricity per hectare per year. A field grown for energy gives about $0.010\,\text{GWh}$ of electricity per hectare per year in a power plant. (The figures are rounded example values; $1\,\text{ha} = 0.01\,\text{km}^2$.) How many times as large a field area would biomass electricity need compared with the area of the solar park? What does land use tell you about the ways of producing energy that the emission factor does not?

Example situation: a city bus uses $30$ litres of diesel per $100\,\text{km}$ and has $25$ passengers. The energy content of diesel is $36\,\text{MJ/}\textsf{l}$ and the emission factor of burning is $74\,\text{g/MJ}$. A petrol car driven by one person uses $6.0$ litres per $100\,\text{km}$ ($32\,\text{MJ/}\textsf{l}$ and $69\,\text{g/MJ}$). How many times as large is the emission from burning of the car per passenger compared with that of the bus?
